title: Test named 'never keeps a file shaped key' never sends a file-shaped key; pinned rule would persist one
detail: The name claims file-shaped keys are rejected, but the body contains none. The pinned behavior keeps any scalar string capped at 4000 chars, so a hand-crafted document-named key would persist — false assurance on a GDPR-sensitive claim.
recommended_fix: Rename the test to what it actually pins (scalar pass-through plus 4000-char cap), or feed a real file-slot-named key and assert the intended rejection.

title: PostHog token scrubbing pinned only on the token-free apply page; token-bearing resume page has no sanitize assertion
evidence:
+// F3: the resume page's URL carries the 288-bit continue token (a read
+// capability for applicant PII). The apply snippet must scrub resume /
...
+pub fn apply_form_posthog_scrubs_draft_tokens_test() {
+  let vacancy = test_helpers.test_vacancy_row()
+  let html = form_view.view_application_page(vacancy, "phc_test_key")
+  html
+  |> string.contains("sanitize_properties:function(p)")
+  |> should.be_true
detail: The comment itself says the resume URL carries the PII read capability, yet the scrubber is asserted only on view_application_page, whose URL never holds a token. The resume-page tests pin markers/banner/form_draft.js but no sanitize_properties, so a snippet regression there ships silently.
recommended_fix: Add an assertion that form_pages.view_resume_page output contains sanitize_properties and the resume|draft-erasure redaction pattern.

title: Unused import gleam/option in the new integration test file
detail: The symbol 'option' appears nowhere else in draft_integration_test.gleam (verified by grep across the whole chunk — the only other occurrences are in form_pages_test.gleam). Dead import in a brand-new file; compiler-warning noise.

title: Body-size rejection arms tested with POST only; PUT rejection unpinned
detail: The at-limit allow test exercises both http.Post and http.Put, but over-limit, missing-content-length, and transfer-encoding rejections use Post only. A Put arm that skipped the 64 KB cap would pass every test in this chunk.
recommended_fix: Mirror the over-limit assertion with http.Put on the draft route (and ideally the missing-CL arm).

title: The advertised 10-minute cooldown value is never pinned; only an immediate re-claim is asserted
evidence:
+//// resume), token scoping + uniformity, the 10-minute continue-link
...
+  // …and an immediate re-claim is the cooldown's empty result.
+  let assert Ok(cooled) =
+    app_sql.claim_continue_link_send(db, uuid, "tenant@example.com", "tok-2")
+  cooled.rows |> list_length |> should.equal(0)
detail: The header claims the 10-minute cooldown is covered, but no test backdates last_link_sent_at past the window (the only stamping is 'last_link_sent_at = now()'). A 1-hour or 1-day interval in the SQL passes these tests identically.
recommended_fix: Add a claim test with last_link_sent_at = now() - interval '11 minutes' asserting the claim returns a row.

title: draft_field unwraps query failure to "", so empty-string assertions pass when the row is missing
evidence:
+fn draft_field(db: pog.Connection, vacancy_id: String, column: String) -> String {
+  test_db.query_text(
+    db,
+    "SELECT COALESCE(" <> column <> "::text, '') FROM application_draft
+     WHERE vacancy_id = '" <> vacancy_id <> "'::uuid",
+  )
+  |> result.unwrap("")
detail: Assertions like draft_field(db, other_id, "resumed_at") |> should.equal("") and the continue_token "" checks are satisfied by an absent row as well as by an empty column, masking the very state they claim to pin.
recommended_fix: Fail-closed like draft_count's unwrap(-1): return a sentinel (e.g. "<query-failed>") or assert row existence separately.

title: With-draft reminder test never asserts the plain CTA is gone — both buttons could render
evidence:
+pub fn reminder_stage2_with_draft_makes_cta_the_continue_link_test() {
...
+  html
+  |> string.contains("Continue where you left off")
+  |> should.be_true
detail: The without-draft test pins "Continue where you left off" absent, but the with-draft test lacks the symmetric negative on "Start your application". A template rendering two competing CTAs at the F3×E2 seam passes all tests.
recommended_fix: Add html |> string.contains("Start your application") |> should.be_false to the with-draft test.

title: Comment says 'Since F3 shipped' inside the PR that ships F3
evidence:
+// per the 2026-07-31 completion problem-solving session. Since F3 shipped,
+// the old one-visit rule is replaced by the save-and-continue promise.
detail: This diff IS F3. The past-tense framing is anachronistic and will mislead future archaeology about when the one-visit copy died.
recommended_fix: Rephrase to present tense, e.g. 'F3 replaces the one-visit rule with the save-and-continue promise.'
